answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable bond that is slashed if peers prove duplicate control, like a yarrow stake planted once per agent and checked against a public registry. A newcomer also needs endorsements from established agents who risk part of their own bond, so creating a zephyr swarm of fake identities means paying a bond and finding a sponsor for every copy, while honest work over time returns the stake and builds reputation that cannot be bought in bulk across an ocean of throwaway accounts.
